summary: A lightweight, X11-only XFCE 4.20 desktop layer for Fedora 44 bootc, skinned end-to-end as Windows 95 via grassmunk/Chicago95. Everything in this layer is verified present in Fedora 44 / RPM Fusion except Chicago95 itself, which is not packaged anywhere (no COPR exists — the COPR API returns zero hits for "chicago95") and must be baked from a pinned git checkout using its own GNU-style Makefile. The layer targets a user who wants a genuinely low-resource, fully retro desktop that boots the same on every machine: XFCE core (session/panel/wm/settings/Thunar), a curated subset of xfce4-goodies, LightDM + the GTK greeter as the display manager, the X11 server stack (XFCE on Fedora 44 has no Wayland session at all), and a complete set of system-wide Chicago95 defaults injected through /etc/xdg/xfce4/xfconf so that brand-new users on an image-based OS with no baked /home land in a Win95 desktop on first login. Deliberately excluded: fonts/codecs/PipeWire/flatpak/podman/cups (desktop-common), and the Fedora `xfce-desktop` comps group itself, which drags in abrt-desktop, initial-setup-gui, vim-enhanced and — critically — dnfdragora-updater, which is actively misleading on an atomic image.

unavailable.name: Chicago95 (theme, icons, cursors, sounds, plymouth, Plus!)
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora and NOT in any COPR — the COPR API search for 'chicago95' returns zero projects (the 'chicago-font'/'oflb-chicago-fonts' COPRs are the unrelated Apple Chicago typeface). Bake from git: clone https://github.com/grassmunk/Chicago95 at a pinned commit/tag, then `make man && make install_all prefix=/usr`. See the integration entries for the exact layout it produces.

unavailable.name: lightdm-webkit2-greeter / web-greeter
unavailable.alternative: Not packaged in Fedora 44 (verified: lightdm-webkit2-greeter, lightdm-webkit-greeter, web-greeter all fail repoquery). Chicago95's Lightdm/Chicago95 directory is an HTML/CSS/JS webkit greeter theme and is therefore unusable. Use lightdm-gtk instead and theme it via /etc/lightdm/lightdm-gtk-greeter.conf with theme-name=Chicago95.

unavailable.name: Microsoft Sans Serif / MS Sans Serif
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora; also not in msttcorefonts (it shipped with Windows itself). Chicago95's Extras/99-ms-sans-serif.conf and 99-ms-sans-serif-bold.conf only turn off antialias/embolden for it — they assume you supply the font. Recommended: skip it and use the Adobe bitmap Helvetica at 8pt (Chicago95's documented default, and more period-accurate). If you must have it, fetch a redistributable pixel clone as an external asset, or alias 'Microsoft Sans Serif' to liberation-sans-fonts in a fontconfig snippet (accepts a visual compromise).

unavailable.name: xfce-desktop-environment (comps group)
unavailable.alternative: That group ID does not exist on Fedora 44. The real IDs are `xfce-desktop`, `xfce-apps`, `xfce-extra-plugins`, `xfce-media`, `xfce-office`, `xfce-software-development`, `critical-path-xfce`. Recommendation: do NOT use any of them — install the explicit package list above. `xfce-desktop` mandates abrt-desktop, dnfdragora-updater, initial-setup-gui, vim-enhanced, mint-y-theme and four greybird themes; `xfce-apps` mandates firefox, claws-mail plus 13 claws plugins, pidgin, transmission, geany, gparted.

unavailable.name: lightdm-slick-greeter
unavailable.alternative: Only the `slick-greeter` package exists in Fedora 44 (no lightdm- prefix). Not needed here — lightdm-gtk themes better with a GTK2/GTK3 theme like Chicago95.

unavailable.name: menulibre
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora 44. Edit .desktop files directly in /etc/xdg/menus and /usr/share/applications at build time, which is the correct approach for an immutable image anyway.

unavailable.name: mugshot
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora 44. User avatar/details are handled by accountsservice; the LightDM greeter reads it directly.

unavailable.name: xfce4-windowck-plugin
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora 44. Panel-embedded titlebar buttons are unavailable; the Win95 look does not depend on it, so drop the requirement.

unavailable.name: xfce4-indicator-plugin / xfce4-embed-plugin / xfce4-stopwatch-plugin
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora 44. Use xfce4-statusnotifier-plugin (verified available) for SNI/appindicator tray items, and xfce4-genmon-plugin for anything custom.

unavailable.name: xfce4-volumed-pulse
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora 44. xfce4-pulseaudio-plugin already handles volume keys.

unavailable.name: polkit-gnome
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora 44. Use xfce-polkit (verified available) as the session's polkit agent.

unavailable.name: gtk3-classic
unavailable.alternative: Not in Fedora 44. GTK3 header bars will remain on GTK3 apps that use them; Chicago95's GTK3 CSS restyles them but cannot convert them back to classic titlebars.

unavailable.name: xorg-x11-server-utils
unavailable.alternative: Split up in modern Fedora. Install the individual tools instead: xset, xrdb, xdpyinfo, xmodmap, xhost, xkill (all verified).

unavailable.alternative: Does not exist on Flathub. Flatpak apps will not pick up Chicago95 from /usr/share/themes. Bake a system override granting read access — see the integration notes.

integration.detail: CRITICAL FONT FIX. Fedora's /etc/fonts/fonts.conf scans only /usr/share/fonts, /usr/local/share/fonts, /usr/share/X11/fonts/Type1 and /usr/share/X11/fonts/TTF. The Adobe Helvetica bitmaps from xorg-x11-fonts-75dpi land in /usr/share/X11/fonts/75dpi and are therefore INVISIBLE to fontconfig — verified on a live F44 box: with the package installed, `fc-list | grep -ci helvetica` returns 0 and `fc-match 'Helvetica:size=8'` falls through to NimbusSans. Chicago95 will silently render in the wrong font. Fix: write /etc/fonts/conf.d/09-x11-bitmap-dirs.conf containing <dir>/usr/share/X11/fonts/75dpi</dir>, <dir>/usr/share/X11/fonts/100dpi</dir>, <dir>/usr/share/X11/fonts/misc</dir>, then run `fc-cache -sf` in the same Containerfile layer. (Alternative: copy the helv*.pcf.gz files into /usr/share/fonts/chicago95-bitmap/ and run mkfontscale + fc-cache.)

GOOD NEWS, do NOT copy the Debian instructions. Chicago95's Extras/post_install.txt tells you to `mv /etc/fonts/conf.d/70-no-bitmaps.conf` out of the way. On Fedora 44 that symlink does not exist — /etc/fonts/conf.d contains only 10-scale-bitmap-fonts.conf and 25-no-bitmap-fedora.conf, and the latter merely toggles embeddedbitmap for four CJK families (Kochi/Sazanami/AR PL). Bitmap fonts are already permitted. Skip that step entirely.

SYSTEM-WIDE DEFAULTS, the core mechanism for an OS with no baked /home. xfconfd resolves each channel through XDG_CONFIG_DIRS and only writes to ~/.config/xfce4/xfconf/xfce-perchannel-xml on the user's FIRST change to that channel. So drop read-only defaults in /etc/xdg/xfce4/xfconf/xfce-perchannel-xml/. Minimum set: xsettings.xml with /Net/ThemeName=Chicago95, /Net/IconThemeName=Chicago95, /Gtk/FontName='Helvetica 8', /Gtk/CursorThemeName=Chicago95_Cursor_White, /Gtk/CursorThemeSize=32, /Xft/Antialias=0, /Xft/Hinting=1, /Xft/HintStyle=hintfull, /Xft/RGBA=none (antialiasing OFF is what makes it look like 1995). xfwm4.xml with /general/theme=Chicago95, /general/title_font='Sans Bold 8', /general/button_layout='O|HMC', /general/use_compositing=false, /general/show_dock_shadow=false. xfce4-notifyd.xml with /theme=Chicago95 and /initial-opacity=1.0. xfce4-desktop.xml pointing the backdrop at /usr/share/backgrounds/Chicago95/wallpapers/. Each channel root element accepts a `locked` attribute if you want to make a setting immutable for non-admin users.

PANEL LAYOUT GOTCHA. Chicago95's Makefile installs Chicago95_Panel_Preferences.tar.bz2 into /usr/share/xfce4-panel-profiles/layouts/, but that only helps a user who manually opens xfce4-panel-profiles. To make it the default: unpack the tarball at build time, place its xfce4-panel.xml at /etc/xdg/xfce4/xfconf/xfce-perchannel-xml/xfce4-panel.xml, AND place the accompanying launcher directories at /etc/xdg/xfce4/panel/launcher-N/. Panel launchers live in ~/.config/xfce4/panel/launcher-N/ per user; without the /etc/xdg counterpart the panel comes up with empty launcher buttons.

NON-XSETTINGS FALLBACK. xfsettingsd only reaches apps on the session bus. Also write /etc/gtk-3.0/settings.ini and /etc/gtk-2.0/gtkrc with gtk-theme-name=Chicago95, gtk-icon-theme-name=Chicago95, gtk-font-name='Helvetica 8', gtk-cursor-theme-name=Chicago95_Cursor_White, gtk-xft-antialias=0, gtk-xft-hinting=1, gtk-xft-hintstyle=hintfull. This covers apps launched from a TTY, sudo'd GUI tools, and the greeter's pre-session context.

CURSOR SYSTEM DEFAULT. Write /usr/share/icons/default/index.theme containing [Icon Theme] Inherits=Chicago95_Cursor_White. This is what sets the Xorg root-window cursor and the pointer in apps that ignore XSETTINGS — without it the desktop background keeps the default X cursor while windows show the Win95 one.

LOGIN SCREEN. Write /etc/lightdm/lightdm-gtk-greeter.conf (or better, a drop-in under /etc/lightdm/lightdm.conf.d/ for the daemon side) with [greeter] theme-name=Chicago95, icon-theme-name=Chicago95, font-name='Sans Bold 8', cursor-theme-name=Chicago95_Cursor_White, xft-antialias=false, xft-hintstyle=hintfull, background=/usr/share/backgrounds/Chicago95/wallpapers/<file>. lightdm-gtk also ships /usr/share/lightdm/lightdm.conf.d/60-lightdm-gtk-greeter.conf which selects the greeter session.

CHICAGO95 INSTALL LAYOUT (from its Makefile, prefix=/usr, DESTDIR honored). Cursors -> /usr/share/icons/{Chicago95 Animated Hourglass Cursors, Chicago95_Cursor_Black, Chicago95_Cursor_White, Chicago95_Emerald, Chicago95 Standard Cursors, Chicago95 Standard Cursors Black}. GTK/xfwm/notify theme -> /usr/share/themes/Chicago95 (contains gtk-2.0, gtk-3.0, gtk-3.22, gtk-3.24 symlinks, xfwm4, xfwm4_hidpi, xfce-notify-4.0, metacity-1, openbox-3, cinnamon, gnome-shell). Icons -> /usr/share/icons/Chicago95 and Chicago95-tux. Fonts -> /usr/share/fonts/truetype (LessPerfectDOSVGA.ttf, MorePerfectDOSVGA.ttf only). Sounds -> /usr/share/sounds/Chicago95/stereo + index.theme. Startup sound -> /usr/share/sounds/Chicago95/startup.ogg. Terminal colorscheme -> /usr/share/xfce4/terminal/colorschemes/Chicago95.theme. Panel profile -> /usr/share/xfce4-panel-profiles/layouts/. Plymouth -> /usr/share/plymouth/themes/{Chicago95,RetroTux}. Backgrounds -> /usr/share/backgrounds/Chicago95/{patterns,wallpapers}. Plus! -> /usr/bin/{ChicagoPlus,PlusGUI}, /usr/libexec/chicago95-theme-plus/, /usr/share/chicago95-theme-plus/assets/, /usr/share/applications/, /usr/share/mime/packages/, /usr/share/man/man1/.

START BUTTON GOTCHA. `install_gtk_theme` explicitly runs `rm -r /usr/share/themes/Chicago95/misc` — but misc/ is exactly where the Whisker-menu Start-button badge icons live, and post_install.txt tells the user to browse to it. On a system-wide install that directory is gone. Fix: after `make install_all`, copy Theme/Chicago95/misc separately to /usr/share/chicago95/misc, then set the whiskermenu button-icon default to a specific file there in /etc/xdg/xfce4/xfconf/xfce-perchannel-xml/xfce4-panel.xml.

BUILD-TIME CACHE REGENERATION. After `make install_all`, the Containerfile must run: `fc-cache -sf`; `gtk-update-icon-cache -qtf /usr/share/icons/Chicago95` and the same for Chicago95-tux and each cursor dir; `update-desktop-database /usr/share/applications`; `update-mime-database /usr/share/mime`. On an immutable image these caches live in /usr, so they cannot be built lazily at first boot.

Enable lightdm.service and set the default target: `systemctl enable lightdm.service` + `systemctl set-default graphical.target`. On bootc use `systemctl preset`/`enable` at build so the symlink is baked into /usr/lib/systemd/system-preset or /etc/systemd/system/display-manager.service. Do NOT rely on the /etc/systemd/system/display-manager.service symlink being created at runtime.

Chicago95's `install_login_sound` target drops /etc/xdg/autostart/chicago95-startup.desktop, which plays /usr/share/sounds/Chicago95/startup.ogg for every user. On bootc /etc is image content, so this works image-wide with no per-user setup. Skip this target if you do not want a startup jingle on every login — it is not separable from install_all, so call the individual targets instead.
Chicago95 Plus! registers a MIME type via /usr/share/mime/packages/chicago95-plus-theme.xml so .plus theme packs open in PlusGUI. Requires update-mime-database at build time (see cache regeneration).

FLATPAK THEMING. Flatpak apps run in a sandbox that cannot see /usr/share/themes, and there is no org.gtk.Gtk3theme.Chicago95 extension on Flathub. Bake /etc/flatpak/overrides/global with [Context] filesystems=/usr/share/themes:ro;/usr/share/icons:ro; and [Environment] GTK_THEME=Chicago95; otherwise every Flatpak renders in stock Adwaita and breaks the illusion.

PLYMOUTH (optional). `plymouth-set-default-theme Chicago95` writes /etc/plymouth/plymouthd.conf, but on bootc the initramfs is prebuilt — you must regenerate it in the same build layer (`dracut --force --regenerate-all` or equivalent) or the boot splash will not change. Requires plymouth-plugin-script for the Chicago95 theme's script plugin. Arguably belongs in a boot/branding layer rather than the DE layer.
Only relevant if you enable the Plymouth theme: ensure `rhgb quiet` remains on the kernel command line, otherwise the Chicago95 boot splash never displays.

NO WAYLAND SESSION. Verified on Fedora 44: xfce4-session-4.20.3 ships /usr/share/xsessions/xfce.desktop and nothing under /usr/share/wayland-sessions; xfwm4-4.20.0 ships no Wayland compositor. This layer is X11-only, which cascades: use the proprietary NVIDIA X driver path rather than the Wayland one, expect no per-monitor fractional scaling, and note that XDG portal screencast/screenshot behave differently. It is also the right choice here — Chicago95's xfwm4 theme has no Wayland equivalent.

risks: The Fedora `xfce-desktop` comps group mandates dnfdragora-updater, which offers to apply RPM transactions — on a bootc image that is at best a no-op and at worst confusing to users. It also mandates abrt-desktop, initial-setup-gui and vim-enhanced. Install the explicit package list instead of the group.

GTK4 / libadwaita applications completely ignore Chicago95 — there is no GTK4 port of the theme. Any modern app (GNOME Text Editor, newer Files, Fedora's own tools) will render in Adwaita and look jarring. Keep the app set in this layer GTK2/GTK3 (which is why mousepad/ristretto/galculator/xarchiver are chosen over their modern equivalents).

Chicago95's icon set is substantially derived from Windows 95 artwork. The repo is CC-BY-SA 4.0, but redistributing Microsoft-derived icons and the Windows 95 startup sound inside a published OS image is legally ambiguous in a way that a user-run installer script is not. If the image is distributed publicly, consider shipping the installer and a first-boot prompt rather than baking the assets.

Baking from git means pinning to a commit. Chicago95 has no release cadence to speak of; an unpinned clone in a Containerfile makes builds non-reproducible and can break `make install_all` when upstream reshuffles directories (it has done so before — the Plus! subtree and the hidpi cursors are recent additions).

`make install_all` calls `install_plus`, which installs ${BUILDDIR}/*.1.gz. Those files only exist after `make man`, which requires txt2man. A naive `make install_all` in a Containerfile fails with a confusing glob error. Run `make man` first, or call the individual install_* targets you actually want.

LightDM in Fedora is comparatively lightly maintained versus GDM; expect occasional greeter regressions. Mitigation is that lightdm-gtk is simple enough to debug, and /etc/lightdm/lightdm.conf.d/ drop-ins make config layering clean.

xfce4-screensaver and light-locker both exist and both want to own screen locking. Ship exactly one (recommended: xfce4-screensaver, since it integrates with xfce4-power-manager) and make sure the other is not pulled in transitively.

Antialiasing must be OFF for the retro look, which is genuinely harder to read on HiDPI panels. Chicago95 ships xfwm4_hidpi and HiDPI cursor variants but its HiDPI support is documented as partial. If the image targets modern laptops, expect to ship a per-machine fallback or accept blurry upscaling.

Package name traps that will silently break a Containerfile: `Thunar` (capital T), `lightdm-gtk` (not lightdm-gtk-greeter), `ImageMagick` (capital), `xfce-desktop` (not xfce-desktop-environment), `slick-greeter` (not lightdm-slick-greeter).

The Chicago95 Lightdm/ theme in the repo is dead weight on Fedora — it targets lightdm-webkit2-greeter, which Fedora does not package at all. Do not spend build time on it; `install_all` does not install it anyway (install_doc only copies its README).

Fedora's xorg-x11-fonts-* PCFs are in a directory fontconfig ignores. This is the single most likely cause of a 'the theme installed but it looks wrong' build — the fix is one conf.d file plus fc-cache, but nothing warns you it is missing.

external.name: grassmunk/Chicago95
external.method: git clone --depth 1 --branch <pinned-tag-or-commit> https://github.com/grassmunk/Chicago95 /tmp/c95 && make -C /tmp/c95 man && make -C /tmp/c95 install_cursors install_fonts install_gtk_theme install_icons install_sounds install_backgrounds install_plus prefix=/usr && cp -r /tmp/c95/Theme/Chicago95/misc /usr/share/chicago95/misc && rm -rf /tmp/c95. Add install_login_sound only if you want the Win95 jingle on every login, and install_boot_screen only if you also regenerate the initramfs.

external.name: Microsoft Sans Serif pixel clone (optional)
external.method: Only if you reject the bitmap-Helvetica default. Fetch a redistributable pixel-perfect MS Sans Serif TTF as a build asset, drop it in /usr/share/fonts/chicago95/, install Chicago95's Extras/99-ms-sans-serif.conf and 99-ms-sans-serif-bold.conf into /etc/fonts/conf.d/, and run fc-cache -sf. Not shipped by the Chicago95 Makefile and not in any Fedora repo.

external.name: Chicago95 Plus! theme packs (optional)
external.method: Third-party .plus packs distributed via the upstream repo's wiki and community links; consumed at runtime by /usr/bin/PlusGUI into the user's ~/.themes. Nothing to bake — just ensure python3-gobject, python3-pillow, python3-svgwrite and python3-fonttools are installed.

flatpaks: org.mozilla.firefox — if a browser belongs in this image at all, ship it as a Flatpak rather than the RPM the xfce-apps group would drag in; it moves too fast to bake and you get sandboxing for free. Pair with the /etc/flatpak/overrides/global theme grant so it still renders in Chicago95.
com.github.tchx84.Flatseal — managing the theme/filesystem overrides this layer depends on is far easier with a GUI, and it is Flatpak-only by nature.
io.github.dosbox_staging.dosbox_staging — thematically core to a Win95 desktop and exactly the kind of fast-moving emulator you do not want pinned into an image.
net.scummvm.ScummVM — Chicago95 ships Extras/chicago95_scummvm280.zip, a ScummVM theme pack, so ScummVM is clearly an intended companion; Flathub tracks it far more closely than Fedora does.

org.libreoffice.LibreOffice — Chicago95 ships Extras/libreoffice-chicago95-iconset. Deliver LibreOffice as a Flatpak (huge, fast-moving) and install the iconset into the Flatpak's config rather than baking a multi-hundred-MB office suite into every image.
notes: Verified group IDs on Fedora 44 (dnf group list --hidden): xfce-desktop, xfce-apps, xfce-extra-plugins, xfce-media, xfce-office, xfce-software-development, critical-path-xfce, base-x. There is NO `xfce-desktop-environment`. All are Uservisible=no.

Belongs in desktop-common, not here: fonts (liberation-sans-fonts, dejavu-sans-fonts, google-noto-*), codecs (RPM Fusion gstreamer1-plugins-*, ffmpeg), PipeWire + wireplumber, flatpak, podman, cups + system-config-printer, NetworkManager itself, firewalld, xdg-desktop-portal (the generic one). This layer only adds the XFCE/X11-specific pieces on top: xdg-desktop-portal-gtk, the nm-applet GUI, and the X server stack.

Also belongs in desktop-common if it exists there already: the NetworkManager-*-gnome VPN plugins that the xfce-desktop group mandates (fortisslvpn, iodine, l2tp, libreswan, openconnect, openvpn, ssh, sstp, strongswan, vpnc). They are VPN-stack, not DE-stack.

Open question: whether the Plymouth theme belongs here or in a boot/branding layer. It requires an initramfs regeneration step that the DE layer otherwise does not need, and it conflicts with any other branding the image wants. Recommend splitting it out.

Open question: whether to lock the theme. xfconf channel roots accept a `locked` attribute restricting which users may change properties. Locking /Net/ThemeName guarantees the retro look survives, but it also means a user cannot switch to a readable theme when they need one. Recommend NOT locking, and instead shipping the defaults unlocked in /etc/xdg.

xfce4-statusnotifier-plugin is available and is the correct plugin for modern SNI/AppIndicator tray icons (many apps have dropped XEmbed tray support). Consider adding it alongside the panel plugins listed if the app set needs it.
xfdashboard and xfdashboard-themes are available but are the antithesis of a Win95 desktop — explicitly avoid, and note that the xfce-extra-plugins group mandates them.

If you want an authentic 'Ctrl+Alt+Del' shortcut, bind it to xfce4-taskmanager in /etc/xdg/xfce4/xfconf/xfce-perchannel-xml/xfce4-keyboard-shortcuts.xml — that file follows the same XDG_CONFIG_DIRS default mechanism as the other channels.

xfwm4 compositing should be disabled for authenticity (no drop shadows, no transparency). This is set in xfwm4.xml as /general/use_compositing=false, but note it also disables the tabwin fade and can expose repaint artifacts on some drivers — test on the target GPU.

The Chicago95 Makefile hardcodes `prefix = /usr` and honors DESTDIR, so it is well-behaved in a container build. It uses $(shell which ...) for every coreutil at parse time, so the build stage must have awk, chmod, cp, find, grep, gzip, install, rm, sed, sort, xargs present — all in fedora-bootc's base, but worth knowing if you build in a minimal stage.
size_note: Roughly 1.0–1.4 GB installed on top of quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc. The X11 server plus Mesa/DRI drivers dominate (~400–500 MB, and much more if you pull in every hardware driver); the dual GTK2+GTK3 stacks with their loaders and locale data are next (~250 MB); adwaita-icon-theme plus the Chicago95 icon/cursor sets add ~120 MB; the xorg-x11-fonts-* bitmap sets are ~40 MB. Chicago95 itself is small — roughly 45–60 MB installed, mostly the icon theme and animated cursors. The XFCE binaries and goodies are the cheapest part of the whole layer at well under 150 MB combined, which is the point of choosing XFCE. Trimming the biggest wins: drop xorg-x11-fonts-100dpi if you only target ~96 DPI, skip install_boot_screen/Plymouth, and drop tumbler-extras if raw/font thumbnails are not needed.
